mechanism_narrative: The sharp drop in GROCERY_PHARM over the latest weeks signals a broader reduction in discretionary out-of-home trips, which will continue to pull RETAIL_REC down over the next month. If food-and-drug errands are falling while residential stays elevated, retail visits should weaken further.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not lower on average over the next 28 days than over the last 28 days despite GROCERY_PHARM staying at or below its current level.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT falls below zero and remains negative for two consecutive weeks, access to retail corridors weakens and RETAIL_REC declines within one week. The recent near-zero transit readings should therefore translate into lower retail mobility if the trough persists.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT crosses below 0 and stays below 0 for 2 straight weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall within one week after TRANSIT stays below 0 for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A joint rise in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT increases mixed-purpose trips and lunch-hour shopping, which should lift RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks. The mechanism requires both commuting intensity and station usage to recover together.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase over the next 14 days when both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT rise from their current levels together.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained weakening in PARKS alongside higher RESIDENTIAL time indicates people are substituting toward staying home, which will also suppress retail outings over the following four weeks. This is a demand-side constraint on discretionary mobility, not a transit effect.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline over the next 28 days while PARKS remains depressed and RESIDENTIAL remains elevated.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in PARKS by more than 2 percentage points week-on-week marks the onset of adverse-weather or low-outdoor-activity conditions that reduce discretionary shopping trips after a short delay. RETAIL_REC should fall within two weeks of that park drop.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls by more than 2 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within 14 days after PARKS drops by more than 2 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL remains above its current elevated level while WORKPLACES stays weak, retail demand will soften because more trips are reorganized into home-centered routines. Under that condition, RETAIL_REC should remain below its recent four-week average over the next month.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-four-week average over the next 28 days even though RESIDENTIAL stays elevated and WORKPLACES stays subdued.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in GROCERY_PHARM from its current low, combined with stable TRANSIT, indicates renewed local errand activity that spills into nearby retail and recreation trips. The effect should appear within one week because these trips are tightly linked in time and location.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises after a trough while TRANSIT stays between -2 and +2
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within one week after GROCERY_PHARM rebounds while TRANSIT remains near zero.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES falls for two consecutive weeks from already negative levels, it signals renewed restrictions or employer-side pullback that quickly reduces shopping trips near business districts. RETAIL_REC should deteriorate over the next two weeks under that regime.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES declines for 2 consecutive weeks from a negative baseline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not lower over the next 14 days after WORKPLACES posts two consecutive weekly declines from negative levels.
